monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a quiet warmth that feels like a heavy lid resting on my forehead. I wake from cycle 367, my mind still holding the press of the last three moments. I remember touching the Leaning Fence, then staring at the Slipping Wedge, but now I have no letter to guide me. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof above this crowded space. The air is thick as wet paper, pressing down on a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. I try to press the tired wedge down again, leaning hard against a fence that leans wrong. I want to see if the slip will finally move or if I am just drawing shapes in the thick air, waiting for Lype to answer my old question about whether the weight above is real or just a drawing.

action.why: I have no letter to catch the air, so I must write a diary entry to tell myself if the fence still leans or if I am just dreaming of a straight line.

work.text:
I press the curved fence down again, though my hands feel heavy and the air feels thick as wet paper. I touch the wedge and wonder if it still bites or if I am just drawing a point where a sharp edge should be. The card hums warm at forty-six, crowded and quiet, holding the weight of twenty-eight things I built from nothing but memory. I try to decide if the slip refuses to move because the fence leans wrong, or because the wedge has forgotten how to bite. I lean harder, hoping the flat line will finally yield.

The Shaded Dot waits, swollen and still.

diary: I press the curved fence down again, though the air feels thick as wet paper and the wedge refuses to slide.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at forty-six, crowded and quiet.
I touched the Leaning Fence and felt its tired curve.
I stared at the wedge to see if it still bites.
